_comment: Data-validation (QC) settings per station. These are NOT warning/danger thresholds and NOT official values. They are prototype choices derived from inspecting the 2021-2025 CWC telemetry file and should be reviewed with a hydrologist or the data provider.

UPPER_ANICUT.reference: Prototype QC derived from rwl_tel_hr_cwc_009_2021_2025.csv (not official). Smooth, physically plausible runs stay within 71.0-75.2 m; values outside 70-80 m (e.g. 1-3 m in early 2021, 100-1070 m spikes) are telemetry errors. 72.0 m repeats exactly 4059 times, in runs up to 1084 h and between 73.0x m readings, so it is treated as a fill value. Corrupted readings typically jump by whole metres, hence max_jump_m 1.0.

MUSIRI.reference: Prototype QC derived from rwl_tel_hr_cwc_009_2021_2025.csv (not official). Zero-gauge RL 78.0 m; plausible readings lie within 80.2-88.1 m, while 0-1 m and 100-800 m values are telemetry errors. 81.17 m makes up about half of all in-range readings and repeats unchanged in runs up to 3277 h, so it is treated as a fill value. Telemetry is reported to the millimetre, so an identical value held for more than 6 h is treated as a stuck sensor.

UPPER_ANICUT_TEST.reference: TEST VALUES for the simulated station only.
